name: Pueblo of Santa Ana grant (Royce Area 680)
citation: Royce records it as confirmed by the United States on 'Feb. 9, 1876' (scan), 17,361 acres; it is not among the claims in the Act of December 22, 1858, 11 Stat. 374
promises: Royce records the Santa Ana grant as confirmed by the United States, 17,361 acres; the confirming act was not opened in this pass.

The Pueblo Lands Act of 1924 made the United States liable, and directed the Pueblo Lands Board to award compensation, for Pueblo land and water lost through the United States' failure to seasonably prosecute the Pueblo's rights (Section 6).
compensation: The Act of May 31, 1933 authorized $2,908.38 for the Pueblo of Santa Ana in addition to the Pueblo Lands Board's awards, and $846.26 for non-Indian claimants 'within the pueblo of Santa Ana (El Ranchito grant)'. The Act does not say which Santa Ana tract the $2,908.38 concerns.
today: Mountain States Telephone & Telegraph Co. v. Pueblo of Santa Ana, 472 U.S. 237 (1985), concerned a 1928 telephone easement across Santa Ana land and the meaning of Section 17 of the 1924 Act; it is not a finding that this grant was taken. The Pueblo says its reservation today is about 79,000 acres.

nationVoice.summary: The Pueblo says its people returned to the present pueblo site in 1693 and then began acquiring adjacent land for farming, and that the Tamaya reservation today covers about 79,000 acres in Sandoval County.

openQuestions: The date 1886-10-01 in treaties.json is not an event date for this land. Royce prints the Pueblo grants under a block headed 'Oct. 1, Act of Congress, Stat. L. XI, 374'; 11 Stat. 374 is the Act of December 22, 1858, which confirmed the grant. This is land the Pueblo kept, not land it ceded. Not edited. Santa Ana is not one of the claims in 11 Stat. 374; Royce lists it in that block with its own confirmation date.
Royce's scan reads 'Confirmed by U. S. Feb. 9, 1876'; that date and the confirming act were not checked (an Act of February 9, 1869 is a possibility, unverified).

The 1933 Act pays Santa Ana $2,908.38 for land divested under the 1924 Act, but the same Act ties Santa Ana's non-Indian claims to the El Ranchito grant, which Santa Ana acquired separately. Until the Pueblo Lands Board report shows land lost inside Royce Area 680, this record is kept at no-breach-found. Lead: the Board's Santa Ana report and Docket 137 (Zia, Jemez, Santa Ana) findings, which concern aboriginal land.
The statute link in treaties.json (ops.libs.uga.edu) was not used; the Act was read on govinfo.

Audit 2026-11-08 (round 14): no-breach-found confirmed. The Act of May 31, 1933 (read on govinfo) is not counted as a breach for any Pueblo grant: it states no findings and names pueblos, not grants, and the Indian Claims Commission held in 1976 that Congress paid full market value for land lost under the 1924 Act (39 Ind. Cl. Comm. 34).

2026-11-08 sweep: Court of Claims and ICC full text searched for Pueblo, Santa Ana, Santa Ana grant; its Court of Claims appearances are in the Docket 137 aboriginal claim (165 Ct. Cl. 501; 200 Ct. Cl. 601); the ICC aboriginal-title decisions found expressly exclude the confirmed grants (e.g. 30 Ind. Cl. Comm. 234, 1973), so nothing new inside this grant.
